findings.issue_text: **`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:14-17` (`totalPages`)** — `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), this yields `3` instead of the correct `2`. Combined with `currentPage`'s equivalent `floor(offset/limit)+1`, `showingLast` never becomes true on the real last page, so the "next" arrow stays enabled and clicking it fetches `offset=100` against a 100-row set, rendering a bogus empty final page. Should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing `user_count === 0` special case kept).

**`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:26-38` (`removeMember` / `addMembers`) and `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6` (`addMembers` / `removeMember` actions)** — Neither the model methods nor the controller actions attach a `.catch`/error handler to the ajax promise chain. Since the backend legitimately returns 422 for automatic groups or invalid saves, and `render_json_error` for validation failures, any such failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no user-facing feedback — the admin sees nothing happen and has no idea the operation failed.

**`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` (test coverage gap)** — No spec exists for `GroupsController#members` (the new `{members:, meta:{total,limit,offset}}` envelope), and no JS test coverage exists at all for the pagination/offset-clamping logic in `Group#findMembers`, despite this being the core of "proper handling of group memberships." Also missing: `add_members`/`remove_member` with a non-existent username/user_id (previously covered "silently succeeds" cases are now unverified).

**`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` and `app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js`** — `setupController` now fires `model.findMembers()` without returning/chaining the promise. Previously `afterModel` returned this promise so Ember's route transition (and loading substate) waited for members to load. Now the transition completes immediately and the member list populates asynchronously after render — likely an intentional UX simplification, but it silently drops the "loading" state guarantee the old code provided; worth confirming there's no flash-of-empty-list regression, especially on slower connections.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1`** — `{{#unless automatic}}` inside the `group-member` itemView template is rendered per-item; depending on how Ember resolves context for `itemView`-based `{{each}}` in this codebase's Ember version, `automatic` could resolve against the member (`User`) object rather than the parent `Group`, which has no such property. If that's the case the remove (×) link would render even for automatic-group members (backend would still reject the request with a silent failure per the issue above). Worth a quick manual QA check against an automatic group (e.g. "admins") to confirm the remove link is actually hidden.

**`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:16`** — `findMembers` now returns `undefined` for an empty name instead of the previous `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`, changing the method's contract from "always returns a promise" to "sometimes returns undefined." No current caller chains on the return value in a way that breaks, but it's a latent footgun for future callers.

**`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:57`** (`addMembers` action) — has a `// TODO: should clear the input` left in place; minor incomplete UX polish for a PR framed as a fix.

**`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-33`** — `limit`/`offset` are taken directly from `params` and used unvalidated in the query. Any (non-admin, only `guardian.ensure_can_see!`) caller can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` to defeat the new default page size, or a malformed/negative value that could surface as an unhandled `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`. Low severity since it's read-only membership data, but worth clamping (e.g. `limit = [limit, 200].min`).

Stylistic: `protected`/`private` method bodies in `admin/groups_controller.rb` and `groups_controller.rb` are now indented two spaces relative to the rest of the class, inconsistent with the surrounding flush-left style — cosmetic only.

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

Low severity since it's read-only membership data, but worth clamping (e.g. `limit = [limit, 200].min`).

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb), the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses them directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping or validation: a client who can hit this endpoint (only gated by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`) can supply an arbitrarily large `limit` to force large queries, and can supply negative or otherwise malformed values (e.g. `offset=-5` -> `to_i` => -5) which can lead to database errors (e.g. negative OFFSET in PostgreSQL) and potentially an unhandled `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`/500. The finding is grounded in the new code introduced by the diff and is a real correctness/robustness issue (and mild DoS risk).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce inconsistent indentation in Ruby controllers: in `admin/groups_controller.rb`, the `can_not_modify_automatic` method is indented under `protected` (extra spaces), and in `groups_controller.rb`, `find_group` is similarly indented under `private`. However, this is purely a formatting/style inconsistency and does not affect behavior, correctness, or security. Under the given criteria, a cosmetic style nit is not a “real problem.”
